name: libigl
listed_description: Simple C++ geometry processing library (awesome-cpp, Graphics; licence tag MPL2)
reason: README and docs index carry no speed claim. Only numbers found: libigl PR #1895 (Sep 2021, maintainer, 56-core Mac Pro) says ~14x faster remesh_self_intersections and ~7x faster mesh_boolean, but against libigl's own previous mutex-heavy code, not another library, with no inputs or methodology. The 6.8x-over-CGAL figure for the SIGGRAPH 2016 Mesh Arrangements method appears only in a secondhand OpenSCAD mailing-list summary (lists.openscad.org, blocked here) and the paper itself was unreachable. Third-party papers (arXiv 2205.14151 'almost 25x faster than libigl') show libigl as the slower baseline. Lead: Zhou et al. SIGGRAPH 2016 Mesh Arrangements paper tables (mesh booleans vs CGAL Nef, Carve) if paper access opens; category would be geometry/meshing, not color-and-resampling.

name: libmpv (mpv)
reason: No numbers in README or in DOCS/man/options.rst (only unquantified 'big speedup' for lavc skip options and a note that zimg may be slower than libswscale). No benchmark repo. The only numeric comparison found is a single user report in VLC issue 25795 (VLC about 6% CPU, mpv under 2%, VLC 3.0.12) seen via a search snippet; code.videolan.org is blocked (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the page could not be opened. Other web claims (10-20% less CPU than VLC at 4K) are from an unsourced blog post. Lead: VLC issue 25795 if videolan.org becomes reachable; it would be tier C anecdote at best.

name: libpng
listed_description: The reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG raster image files (awesome-cpp, Image Processing)
reason: libpng is the reference implementation and the incumbent baseline itself; README and CHANGES make no comparison against another library. Its SIMD filter sources (intel/intel_init.c) say 'about 3x for 3bpp, 4x for 4bpp' as design estimates, not measurements; CHANGES has only a 1998 note (Paeth optimisation, avg decode about 20% faster than libpng 1.0.1) against itself. In the only third-party numeric table found (google/wuffs doc/benchmarks.md, libpng 1.6.37, i5-10210U, Debian gcc 10.2.1/clang 11 builds) libpng is the 1.00x baseline and is slower than libspng and Wuffs and Rust png on most rows; it is ahead of lodepng and stb only on the 4002k 24bpp image (214 MB/s vs 165 and 163 MB/s) and of Go image/png on all rows. Nobody claims libpng is faster, so no record. Lead: Wuffs doc/benchmarks.md is already the evidence source for libspng and Wuffs entries.

name: libsndfile
listed_description: Library for reading and writing sound files (awesome-c, Multimedia; listed URL http://www.mega-nerd.com/libsndfile/, not opened, host not reachable here)
reason: README, NEWS.OLD and CHANGELOG.md carry no speed claim or numbers; 1.0.31 adds an SSE2 psf_lrintf() with no benchmark. Only indirect numbers: faroit/python_audio_loading_benchmark times PySoundFile (libsndfile binding) against scipy, pydub, audioread-FFmpeg, aubio, librosa, but results are chart images with no numeric table or CPU model, the repo's pickled result tables disagree with the PNG charts, FFmpeg is spawned as a subprocess there, and scipy.io.wavfile beats soundfile on WAV. Not a libsndfile-versus-baseline claim. Lead: that benchmark's results/ pickles if someone reruns it with a stated CPU.

name: libsndfile
listed_description: C library with C++ wrapper for reading and writing files containing sampled sound through one standard library interface (awesome-cpp, Audio; listed URL https://github.com/erikd/libsndfile/, the old home of the same project)
reason: Same project as the previous libsndfile entry (erikd/libsndfile moved to libsndfile/libsndfile); same finding, no numeric claim against any baseline.

name: libsoundio
listed_description: Library for cross-platform, real-time audio input and output (awesome-c, Multimedia; listed URL http://libsound.io, not opened)
reason: README says only that the design leans toward performance over API convenience and that raw devices give best performance; no numbers, no PortAudio or other comparison, no benchmark in repo (dirs: cmake, doc, example, soundio, src, test; the test 'latency' program is a beep alignment check). Web searches found no measured latency or CPU comparison with PortAudio or others, only unsourced prose and one user anecdote.

name: libsoundio
listed_description: C library for cross-platform real-time audio input and output (awesome-cpp, Audio; listed URL https://github.com/andrewrk/libsoundio)
reason: Same project as the previous libsoundio entry; same finding, directional design claim only, no numbers.
